question: A 55-year-old man with established IHD (previous STEMI, on statin therapy) has a fasting LDL-C of 1.9 mmol/L (73 mg/dL). According to current ESC/ACC guidelines, what is the appropriate LDL-C target for this very high-risk patient?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This target applies to high-risk patients (e.g., multiple risk factors, diabetes without organ damage). For very high-risk patients with established ASCVD, the target is more stringent.

answers.text: LDL-C < 1.8 mmol/L (70 mg/dL) and ≥50% reduction from baseline

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. For very high cardiovascular risk (established ASCVD, including prior MI, stroke, or peripheral artery disease), the target is LDL-C <1.8 mmol/L (70 mg/dL) AND at least a 50% reduction from untreated baseline. This patient at 1.9 mmol/L is above target.

This ultra-low target (1.4 mmol/L) applies to extreme risk patients — those with a second cardiovascular event within 2 years despite maximally tolerated statin therapy. This patient had a single STEMI.

answers.text: Any LDL-C reduction is acceptable as long as the patient is on statin therapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Statin initiation alone is insufficient — guideline-directed targets must be met. Intensification (higher-dose statin, ezetimibe, or PCSK9 inhibitor) is required if targets are not achieved.

overallFeedback.feedback: LDL targets by risk tier: High risk (<2.6 mmol/L) → Very high risk/established ASCVD (<1.8 mmol/L + ≥50% reduction) → Extreme risk/recurrent events (<1.4 mmol/L + ≥50% reduction).
Excellent. Very high-risk (established ASCVD): LDL-C <1.8 mmol/L AND ≥50% reduction. Extreme risk (recurrent event on max statin): LDL-C <1.4 mmol/L AND ≥50% reduction.
